computer-organisation-and-ports.read: Chapters on processor structure and the memory hierarchy (register organisation, cache and internal memory)
computer-organisation-and-ports.why: The course book lists Stallings for registers, the PSW and the memory hierarchy.

memory-segments-and-assembly-basics.read: Chapters on instruction sets and assembly language
memory-segments-and-assembly-basics.why: Instruction formats, x86 registers and the link between assembly and machine code.

assembly-instructions.read: Chapters on instruction sets: addressing modes and formats
assembly-instructions.why: Register, immediate and memory addressing and the x86 instruction types the course uses.

processes-threads-and-concurrency.why: The course book's thread units are taken from Deitel's multithreading chapter.

java-threads-and-synchronization.why: Thread states, priorities, executors, locks, conditions and the producer/consumer examples, as in the course book.

network-programming-in-java.why: URLs, stream-socket servers and clients and datagram programs; the course book names Java How to Program, Sixth Edition.

unix-processes-and-ipc.read: Chapters 20–28 (signals and process creation) and 43–54 (interprocess communication)
unix-processes-and-ipc.why: fork, exec, vfork, signals, pipes, message queues and shared memory, which the 2024/25 paper asks about.
